sanskrit_verse:
साक्षिलेख्यानुमानं च मानुषी त्रिविधा क्रिया ।
साक्षी द्वादश भेदस् तु लिखितं त्वष्टधा स्मृतम् ॥
transliteration: sākṣilekhyānumānaṃ ca mānuṣī trividhā kriyā / sākṣī dvādaśa bhedas tu likhitaṃ tv aṣṭadhā smṛtam //
sph_interpretive_translation: Testimony, documentary evidence, and inference constitute the threefold human action in establishing facts; witnesses are classified into twelve types, and written records into eight categories.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority of experiential cognition as foundational to legal validity
Causation through witnessed manifestation rather than abstract attribution
Capacity-based responsibility determined by direct knowledge or record
Restoration logic rooted in factual clarity and conscious alignment with truth
Consciousness alignment through verified experiential and documented proof
executable_legal_axioms: IF a claim lacks sākṣi (witness), lekhya (document), or anumāna (inference), THEN it is not admissible as actionable dharma.
IF a witness falls outside the twelve recognized categories, THEN their testimony is not computable within dharmic adjudication.
IF a document does not conform to one of the eight defined classes, THEN it shall not activate legal consequence.
IF inference contradicts sākṣi or lekhya without higher-consciousness validation, THEN it is null for juridical purposes.
ALL evidentiary inputs MUST be mapped to trikāla (past-present-future) experiential integrity before adjudication.
supreme_court_application: At the Supreme Court level, only those testimonies, documents, and inferences that align precisely with the tripartite classification are to be accepted. The threshold of responsibility is established through capacity-based verification against the twelve-fold witness typology and eight-fold documentation schema. Adjudication proceeds only when all three pramāṇas affirm the same causal sequence without contradiction.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa-based causality ensures that no agent is assigned fault beyond their verifiable perceptual or recorded involvement. Anupūrvaśaḥ mandates sequential alignment of cause-effect chains observable through sākṣi, lekhya, or anumāna. Responsibility is proportionally assigned based on clarity of perception and integrity of record, ensuring no punitive overlay distorts the alignment of consciousness with factual reality.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Completion Process: Reconstruct event sequence using valid sākṣi-lekhya-anumāna triad until full factual alignment is achieved.
Responsibility Assumption Protocol: Agent assumes role only where pramāṇa confirms direct causal linkage.
Capacity Restoration Mechanism: Realign individual's cognitive apparatus to perceive truth accurately through guided śāmbhavī meditation.
Integrity Reintegration System: Reestablish societal trust via public declaration of factual restoration and non-recurrence assurance.
final_declaration: By the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands declared: Truth is established through sākṣi, lekhya, and anumāna alone. Dharma is restored through factual clarity, not punitive reaction. Consciousness is the ultimate judge, and reality is inherently non-punitive.
